input.quote: Sparkling shall pay the fees as set out in the Fee Schedule in accordance with the terms of this Agreement and the Fee Schedule.
input.rationale: Full-document sweep confirms Garman has no audit, inspection, records-examination, usage-verification or true-up right against Sparkling, and no right of access to Sparkling systems. Searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "records", "premises", "monitor", "report" and "certif" return nothing operative. Specifically: § 3 Restrictions on Use ((a)-(g)) imposes substantive use limits only, with no compliance-reporting or inspection mechanism; § 11 Fees is a bare payment obligation keyed to the Fee Schedule with no verification, reporting or reconciliation right; § 2 conditions off-site use on "payment of additional fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule" but gives Garman no means to inspect or audit to test that; § 14 Confidentiality mentions "accounting records for which access is obtained" only to bring such records within Confidential Information, not to create access; § 20 General Matters is time-of-the-essence and notices boilerplate. The Schedules (A-F) are listed in § 1 as forming part of the Agreement but are summary-titled only (Fee Schedule, Software/Documentation, Authorized Locations, Specifications, Implementation and Training, Telephone Support) and contain no reporting or verification machinery in the text available. The only certification obligation, § 17(b), is a one-off post-termination self-certification that Software, Documentation and Codes have been destroyed or returned - a customary wind-down confirmation by us, not a recurring vendor audit, and it involves no vendor entry, auditor or system access. Because no audit right binds us, the AUDIT parameters (frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access) do not arise, and this position is at least as favorable as the playbook preferred position. Inserting audit machinery would create a new Customer obligation and enlarge Garman's rights, so the smallest correct edit is none.
